punchline: Marcus Aurelius learned to rule by eating bread and picking grapes beside the emperor who adopted him.
thirty_sec: In 138 Antoninus Pius adopted the teenage Marcus Aurelius as Hadrian had required. A letter Marcus wrote a few years later describes an ordinary day: bread at lunch while others ate beans and herring, then grape-picking beside his father until he sweated. In the Meditations he thanked Antoninus for showing him a ruler could live at court without bodyguards, fancy clothes or statues.
question: Whose ordinary day could you learn from?
